notes: RETURNING is implemented as a pseudo-trigger owned by the Parse object, not by the schema: sqlite3AddReturning() does pRet = sqlite3DbMallocZero(db, sizeof(*pRet)) at src/build.c:1271 in the 658f0a36796b^ tree, and the Returning object embeds the Trigger and its single TriggerStep. It is released once, by the parse cleanup. The generic trigger teardown reached by a corrupt schema, however, called sqlite3DeleteTrigger() on it; the only thing standing in the way was assert( !pTrigger->bReturning ), which is compiled out of a release build, so the object was freed a second time along with its zName/table strings. notes: withExpand() assigned pItem->pTab = pTab and only afterwards incremented pTab->nTabRef, with an error return for 'multiple references to recursive table' in between. On that error path the FROM-clause item holds a pointer that the reference count does not account for, so the Table is deleted once while pItem->pTab still names it and the parse cleanup dereferences it again. The fix moves pTab->nTabRef++ above the error return. The Table here is not a schema object: it is built for the CTE inside query expansion with pTab = sqlite3DbMallocZero(db, sizeof(Table)) in withExpand() -- the function is named resolveFromTermToCte() in 3.53.4, where the same allocation is at src/select.c:5735 -- and query expansion runs on a SELECT, so parse.y's disableLookaside() has not fired and sizeof(Table) is well under db->lookaside.sz -- the freed object is a lookaside slot pushed onto the connection freelist, not a heap block. Distinct from the 2021 use-after-free in the same function fixed by 93c8139c1a9755a9f599, which adds a pParse->nErr guard at function entry; this one is the ordering of pTab->nTabRef++ against the recursive-reference error return.

notes: When a corrupt record runs out of bytes mid-field the unpack loop exits with the last Mem left as the decoder wrote it from out-of-range data, and p->nField still counts it, so callers compare against a Mem whose contents were never validly initialised. The fix calls sqlite3VdbeMemSetNull(pMem-1) when d>nKey. The Mem array is the tail of the UnpackedRecord: sqlite3VdbeAllocUnpackedRecord() computes nByte = ROUND8(sizeof(UnpackedRecord)) + sizeof(Mem)*(pKeyInfo->nKeyField+1) and does p = sqlite3DbMallocRaw(pKeyInfo->db, nByte) (src/vdbeaux.c, 4067ce7d5404^ tree). With sizeof(Mem) around 56 bytes a two- or three-column index needs only a couple of hundred bytes, so the record comes from a lookaside slot and the 'uninitialized' Mem is in fact the residue of whatever object last held that slot.

consequence: silent wrong answer on a corrupt database - an index comparison made against a Mem that holds the residue of the slot's previous occupant. notes: The recheck loop cached pOp = sqlite3VdbeGetOp(v, addrConflictCk) and then called sqlite3VdbeAddOp4() inside the loop while continuing to read and increment pOp. sqlite3VdbeAddOp*() can grow the opcode array in place: growOpArray() does pNew = sqlite3DbRealloc(p->db, v->aOp, nNew*sizeof(Op)) at src/vdbeaux.c:174 in the d901b168b58b^ tree, so the cached pointer is left aimed at the released block. The first opcode array a statement allocates is 1024/sizeof(Op) entries -- 42 entries of 24 bytes, 1008 bytes -- which is inside db->lookaside.sz, so that first growth hands the old block back to the lookaside freelist rather than to realloc's free, and the stale pOp keeps reading a slot that is now on the free list. Once the array has doubled past 1200 bytes the same defect is an ordinary heap use-after-realloc. The fix copies the opcode by value (VdbeOp x = *sqlite3VdbeGetOp(...)) and advances addrConflictCk instead of the pointer.

affected_function: sqlite3EndTable (generated-column expression left in the schema)
notes: A generated-column expression is stored in the schema (Column.pDflt), and the schema is shared and outlives every individual connection, so nothing in it may come from lookaside -- which is why parse.y's createkw action calls disableLookaside() for every CREATE. But when sqlite3ResolveSelfReference() fails on such an expression the tree is left in place and later code generators keep rewriting it, and those rewrites run with the arena live, so fresh Expr nodes from sqlite3ExprAlloc()'s sqlite3DbMallocRawNN(db, sizeof(Expr)+nExtra) (src/expr.c:941 in 3.53.4) get spliced into a schema-resident tree. Upstream's own comment in the fix says so: 'inserting extra parts into the expression tree that have been allocated from lookaside memory, which is illegal in a schema and will lead to errors heap corruption when the database connection closes.' The fix replaces the unresolvable expression with a bare TK_NULL node. When the owning connection closes, its lookaside slab is released by sqlite3_free while the schema still points into it.

Before the fix the schema ends up holding Expr nodes that live in the connection's lookaside slab; nothing faults while that connection is open, because the slots are simply in use. The damage appears when the connection closes and the slab is freed under a schema that still references it, or, in shared-cache, when another connection walks the same schema. No repro recorded: the check-in cites no public testcase, and per this row's own poc field the reproducer lives in the proprietary TH3 suite.

notes: The corruption guard was 'if( unlikely(szHdr<3 || (int)szHdr>m.n) )'. szHdr is a u32 read from the record header; casting it to int makes any value above 0x7fffffff negative, so the guard passes and the routine goes on to decode fields from a header that claims to be longer than the record. The fix compares szHdr>(unsigned)m.n. m is filled by sqlite3VdbeMemFromBtree(pCur, 0, (u32)nCellKey, &m) at src/vdbeaux.c:4551 (44d068532ef5^ tree); when the index key does not fit in the local cell payload that routine takes the vdbeMemFromBtreeResize() path and the key is copied into pMem->zMalloc = sqlite3DbMallocRaw(pMem->db, n), i.e. a lookaside slot for any key up to about 1199 bytes, so the out-of-bounds decode walks into neighbouring slots of the same slab. Keys that fit locally are read directly out of the pager page buffer instead.

notes: Check-in 63d1632f1ef1 removed the zero terminator from the buffer that sqlite3VdbeMemFromBtree() builds for records that spill onto an overflow page, shrinking the request from amt+1 to amt. The record decoders deliberately over-read that buffer by one byte when the record is malformed, so the shrink turned a designed slack byte into a real over-read; this check-in restores it and writes pMem->z[amt] = 0. The buffer is sqlite3VdbeMemClearAndResize(pMem, amt) -> sqlite3VdbeMemGrow -> pMem->zMalloc = sqlite3DbMallocRaw(pMem->db, n) at src/vdbemem.c:163 in the 24ddadfa3bd7^ tree, so for any overflowing record up to about 1199 bytes the one-byte read past the end lands inside the same lookaside slab.

The With object is allocated by sqlite3WithAdd() in src/build.c with pNew = sqlite3DbMallocZero(db, sizeof(*pWith)) and grown with sqlite3DbRealloc(db, pWith, sizeof(*pWith) + sizeof(pWith->a[1])*pWith->nCte) -- a few tens of bytes for a one- or two-CTE clause, so a lookaside slot; the Select objects themselves come from sqlite3DbMallocRawNN(db, sizeof(Select)) in sqlite3SelectNew(). WITH clauses are parsed as part of a SELECT, not a CREATE, so parse.y's disableLookaside() never fires and the arena is live. Freeing the same in-range block twice pushes it onto db->lookaside.pFree twice, producing a freelist that hands the same slot to two live objects; it never reaches free(), so no allocator check sees it.

notes: After reading the record-header size varint the routine set d1 = szHdr1 and started decoding fields without ever checking szHdr1 against nKey1, so a corrupt header size larger than the record sent the first field read past the end of the buffer. The buffer is the index record handed in as pKey1; on the path through sqlite3VdbeIdxKeyCompare / sqlite3VdbeMemFromBtree, a record that spills onto an overflow page is copied into pMem->zMalloc = sqlite3DbMallocRaw(pMem->db, n) (src/vdbemem.c, sqlite3VdbeMemGrow), i.e. into a lookaside slot for any record up to about 1198 bytes, and the over-read then walks into adjacent slots of the same slab. Records small enough to sit in the local cell payload are read straight out of the pager page instead.

notes: Before this check-in the in-memory schema was allocated from whichever connection happened to parse it: sqlite3StartTable() does pTable = sqlite3DbMallocZero(db, sizeof(Table)) at src/build.c:828 in the d9da78a2c893^ tree, and the column names, the Index objects and the default-value Expr trees hang off the same connection's sqlite3DbMalloc* calls. All of those are far under db->lookaside.sz, so the schema physically lived inside one connection's lookaside slab while a Schema outlives the statement that built it and, in shared-cache mode, outlives the connection itself. The release path made the mismatch explicit: freeIndex() and sqlite3DeleteTable() recovered the connection with p->pTable->db, so a second connection tearing down the shared schema pushed blocks onto -- or read blocks belonging to -- an arena that was not its own. The fix replaces Table.db with Table.dbMem (0 whenever the object must not use lookaside) and is the origin of the DisableLookaside mechanism that src/parse.y:139 still fires from createkw for every CREATE statement, and that src/sqliteInt.h:1617 implements by setting db->lookaside.sz=0. Ticket #3743.

affected_function: BETWEEN grammar action in parse.y (sqlite3ExprSpan on already-deleted operands)
notes: The BETWEEN action at src/parse.y:806 (8867e38aab61^ tree) ends with sqlite3ExprSpan(A,&W->span,&Y->span). W and Y have already been handed to sqlite3ExprListAppend() and sqlite3PExpr(), both of which destroy their operands when the allocation they attempt fails -- sqlite3Expr() does sqlite3ExprDelete(db,pLeft) at src/expr.c:394 -- so after a malloc failure &W->span and &Y->span dereference freed Expr nodes. Expr nodes come from sqlite3DbMallocZero(db,sizeof(Expr)) at src/expr.c:388, about 88 bytes, far inside db->lookaside.sz, and sqlite3DbFree() returns an in-range block to the connection freelist instead of calling free(), so the dangling read is silent. Upstream states the blindness directly: the check-in comment says the OOM segfault was 'discovered while using SQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE', and the same check-in adds the SQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE capability flag so lookaside.test can be skipped in that build. || FIX NEVER SHIPPED 2026-09-04: the parse.y guard was removed 29 minutes later by ddecae799, which fixed it differently. git tag --contains claims every tag from 3.6.4 carries it; the content says no release did.

build_config: default; requires an injected malloc failure (the tester's fault-injection harness)
oracle: No SQL-only reproducer: the read happens only when a malloc fails between parsing the BETWEEN operands and the sqlite3ExprSpan() call. With lookaside on, the freed Expr slot is still mapped and its span token still readable, so the parse simply unwinds and the statement returns SQLITE_NOMEM -- indistinguishable from a correct OOM. With SQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE (or sqlite3_db_config_lookaside db 0 0 0) the same fault-injected run segfaults, which is how upstream found it.
discovery_evidence: Check-in 8867e38aab61: 'Fix a OOM segfault in the BETWEEN operator parsing - discovered while using SQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE.' That is the project's own words: the defect surfaced only once the arena was compiled out, in an OOM fault-injection run of the project's own test suite. No sanitizer, valgrind, assert or fuzzer is named, and the same check-in adds the SQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE capability flag so lookaside.test can be skipped in that build - so the routine instrumented run, with the arena ON, did NOT find it.
object_type: Expr (the W and Y operands of the BETWEEN rule, freed by their consumers on OOM)
object_size_pool: single-size pool - lookaside ships from 3.6.1 with one 1200-byte slot class; the small/big split is 3.31.0 and irrelevant here (the small/big split only exists from 3.31.0 (two-size lookaside, LOOKASIDE_SMALL=128)). Expr nodes come from sqlite3DbMallocZero(db, sizeof(Expr)), about 88 bytes in the 2008 tree per this row's own note (72 bytes on LP64 in modern trees), far inside db->lookaside.sz. In 3.0.0-3.6.0 there is no arena at all and the same defect is an ordinary heap use-after-free.
consequence: crash under SQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE, nothing at all with the arena on. Demonstrated: the check-in calls it an 'OOM segfault'. With lookaside on the freed Expr slot is still mapped and its span token still readable, so the parse unwinds and the statement returns SQLITE_NOMEM - indistinguishable from a correct OOM.
